status: CONFIGURATION EVIDENCE FOR A CHAIN WITH NO DEPLOYMENT OF THIS REPOSITORY. Nothing from this repository exists on chain 5042. This file records read-only JSON-RPC measurements taken from Arc mainnet on 2026-09-18, for a deployment that has not been broadcast and is not authorised. It is NOT an address book: if a deployment ever happens, what exists on chain goes in contracts/config/deployments/arc-mainnet.json, written from what the chain returned. Modelled key-for-key on robinhood-mainnet.json so the two diff field by field. THE ROUTER IS NOW RESOLVED AND THE BASKET QUESTION IS ANSWERED - see router and unresolved. What remains open is not a lookup: Arc has a BTC leg and NO ETH leg, so the basket SHAPE is an owner decision. It still cannot be deployed from as it stands.

verifiedOnChain.method: Hand-rolled read-only JSON-RPC (eth_chainId, eth_blockNumber, eth_getBlockByNumber, eth_call, eth_getCode) from Node, with serial reads and backoff. No key, no broadcast, no forge, no cast. Every age and gap below is measured against the chain's OWN block timestamp, never the reader's wall clock.
verifiedOnChain.operationalNote: `eth_getLogs` WORKS ON ARC AND IS CAPPED, NOT REFUSED — corrected 2026-09-18 after this file's first draft claimed otherwise and that claim stalled the basket work for a session. The cap is 10,000 blocks on rpc.mainnet.arc.io and 100,000 on arc.gateway.tenderly.co, and a bounded, address- and topic-filtered scan succeeds: a complete `PoolCreated` sweep from the factory's deploy block to head returned 26,286 pools across 26,187 tokens with ZERO window errors. The original draft read -32012 'requested range too large' from an UNFILTERED Transfer-topic scan at 50,000 and at 900 blocks and generalised it to all log queries; the variable that mattered was the filter, not the window. The Blockscout explorer at explorer.arc.io does still return HTTP 403 to programmatic requests, with or without a browser User-Agent — that part held. THREE MORE ENDPOINTS SERVE ARC: arc.gateway.tenderly.co, 5042.rpc.thirdweb.com and arc.drpc.org (no logs on its free plan), so Arc facts can meet the two-provider cross-check rule rather than resting on one endpoint.
verifiedOnChain.addressSquattingChecked: THE CANONICAL UNISWAP ADDRESSES ON ARC ARE NOT UNISWAP, verified rather than assumed, exactly as robinhood-mainnet.json had to verify the same class of claim. 0x1F98431c8aD98523631AE4a59f267346ea31F984 (canonical UniswapV3Factory) and 0x68b3465833fb72A70ecDF485E0e4C7bD8665Fc45 (canonical SwapRouter02) BOTH carry 2,747 bytes of code on 5042, and both fail to self-identify: owner(), feeAmountTickSpacing(), getPool(), factory() and WETH9() every one returns empty (0x). Neither is an EIP-1967 proxy — both implementation slots are zero. Do not populate `router` from a canonical address on this chain.

usdcNote: GENUINE CIRCLE USDC, and on Arc it is a NATIVE PREDEPLOY rather than a deployed ERC-20 — the same address on every Arc network. Read on 5042: 1,798 bytes of code, decimals() 6, symbol() "USDC", name() "USDC". Unlike robinhood-mainnet.json, where the `usdc` key held USDG, here the key and the asset agree, so `scripts/verify-mainnet-config.mjs`'s symbol()=="USDC" && decimals()==6 assertion passes on both halves. `VaultCore` reads decimals() once and caches usdcScalar = 10**(18-6) = 1e12 immutably, which satisfies the SHORTFALL_DUST_WAD floor.
usdcIsAlsoGasNote: ON ARC THE NATIVE GAS ASSET IS USDC ITSELF, exposed two ways over ONE pool of funds: an 18-decimal native view used only for gas and msg.value, and this 6-decimal ERC-20 view at the address above. They are not two assets and must never be summed, converted or swapped between. Nothing in `contracts/` reads a native balance, so the vault accounting is unaffected — but any off-chain surface that displays a balance must use the 6-decimal ERC-20 view alone. This has no analogue on 4663 or Base and is the single most likely place for an integrator to double-count.

chainlinkOracle.note: The launch oracle path, exactly as on Base and 4663: one genuine Chainlink Data Feed per asset, consumed directly by `ChainlinkOracle`. All four proxies below were read on 5042 and every one returned 9,571 bytes of code, decimals() 8 and version() 6 — the same EACAggregatorProxy shape as the feeds on 4663 — with description() matching the string recorded beside it exactly.
chainlinkOracle.sequencerUptimeFeedNote: NONE SUPPLIED AND NONE FOUND. No L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed appears in Chainlink's published feed set for arc-mainnet (32 feeds, enumerated 2026-09-18), and Arc is an L1 rather than an L2 rollup, so the Base uptime-feed pattern does not apply. This is the SAME EXEMPTION 4663 required, and it is an OWNER DECISION rather than a detail: `DeployChainlinkOracle.s.sol` refuses chains it has no sequencer policy for, and that refusal has to be widened deliberately before any deploy here.
chainlinkOracle.feedsEnumeratedFrom: https://reference-data-directory.vercel.app/feeds-arc-mainnet.json — 32 feeds on arc-mainnet. The same directory returns HTTP 404 for every arc testnet slug tried (arc-testnet, arc), which is the measurement behind `arcTestnetIsNotADeployTarget`.

assets.tokenNote: THE ONLY BASKET-ELIGIBLE NON-STABLE ASSET ON ARC, resolved 2026-09-18 by a complete PoolCreated scan of the real v3 factory - 26,286 pools, 26,187 tokens, zero window errors - not by symbol search. Circle FiatToken stack. symbol() cirBTC, decimals() 8, both re-read on two independent endpoints. Depth: $7.40M USDC against 73.38 BTC in a single pool, which is $7.40M of the $9.43M total USDC across all 25,101 Arc v3 USDC pools. AMM spot $81,272 against the Chainlink feed's $81,110 - 0.20% apart, so the feed and the venue agree.
assets.feedDescriptionNote: POPULATE AND CHECK THIS FIELD - it is the only thing separating the price feed from a proof-of-reserve feed that is otherwise identical. See proofOfReserveTrap.

chainlinkOracle.heartbeatNote: MEASURE THE CADENCE, NOT THE INSTANTANEOUS AGE, AND MEASURE IT OVER A WINDOW LONGER THAN THE HEARTBEAT ITSELF — this file was wrong about that twice, each time by sampling too little, and the second correction was itself overstated. THE WORST GAP IS 86,423 s (24.01 h) ON BTC/USD AND 86,404 s ON CBBTC/USD, and those are the figures to use. Measured by walking getRoundData back on the feeds themselves, 2026-09-18: BTC/USD 199 gaps over a 449 h span, median 4,352 s; CBBTC/USD 199 gaps over 507 h, median 4,531 s. THE FIGURE IS STABLE, NOT STILL CLIMBING, and this file previously said the opposite. The earlier readings of 4.71 h (11 rounds) and 11.94 h (24 rounds) rose only because each window was SHORTER THAN THE HEARTBEAT and so never contained a quiet stretch. Once the window exceeded it the figure stopped moving: a 169 h walk and a 449 h walk both return 86,423 s, and that worst gap sits 2 s above the runner-up rather than standing off as an outlier. Only three of BTC/USD's 199 gaps exceed 86,400 s at all, by +7 s, +21 s and +23 s. THE BOUND IS ONE HEARTBEAT PERIOD PLUS PUBLISH JITTER, and USDC/USD on the same chain is what shows it: 56 gaps, every one between 86,400 s and 86,467 s, publishing on nothing but its heartbeat because a stablecoin resting at 1.0000 never trips a deviation threshold. So the heartbeat configured for this feed family on Arc IS 86,400 s, the BTC feeds reach it, and the jitter around it is real, positive, and reaches +67 s on the best-sampled feed.
chainlinkOracle.usdcFeedNote: A USDC/USD feed exists at 0x84EA90AC252Dc437031461836DB5164219147905 (description "USDC / USD", 8 decimals, version 6, answer 99986742 = $0.99986742). `ChainlinkOracle` does NOT consume it: the settlement token is pinned at 1e18 and is forbidden from the feed map. It is recorded because its round history is the cleanest measurement of the heartbeat itself — a stablecoin resting at 1.0000 never trips a deviation threshold, and its ten measured gaps are 86,404–86,467 s, i.e. it publishes on nothing but the heartbeat. That is the same behaviour USDG/USD showed on 4663.
chainlinkOracle.heartbeatChoiceNote: 90,000 s, SET IN contracts/config/arc-mainnet.json, WHICH NOW EXISTS. This note previously said the file did not exist and that no legal value was safe; both were true before 2026-09-18 and are false now, so they are replaced rather than annotated. WHAT CHANGED IS THE CONTRACT, NOT THE MEASUREMENT: ChainlinkOracle.MAX_HEARTBEAT was raised from 86,400 s to 90,000 s, because the old ceiling sat 23 SECONDS BELOW the worst gap measured above — a vault configured at the contract maximum would have false-tripped inside the preceding two weeks, and oracle staleness reverts every NAV-reading path INCLUDING exits, so a false trip freezes members out of their own funds while the feed is healthy. THE OLD CEILING WAS WRONG IN ITS ARGUMENT, NOT ITS ARITHMETIC: its NatSpec argued 24 h from Chainlink's slowest published heartbeat TIER, and a tier is not a gap — the gap is the tier plus publish jitter, which is strictly positive. 90,000 = 86,400 + 3,600: one hour of jitter allowance, roughly 54x the largest jitter observed in 56 days on USDC/USD. The ceiling is bounded from ABOVE as well, at one heartbeat period over the measured worst gap, pinned in contracts/test/audit/AuditOracleParamBounds.t.sol — a ceiling raised far enough that the staleness guard can never fire leaves that guard present, configured and inert, which is worse than the negative margin it was raised to fix. Raising it further needs a new measurement, not a new opinion. IT SHIPPED WITHOUT AN EXTERNAL RE-AUDIT by owner decision, so the internal verdict is the only review that contract change will ever get. See Decisions/2026-09-18 MAX_HEARTBEAT raised to 90000, and read contracts/config/arc-mainnet.json rather than this file for the live values — this is the raw survey, the config is what was built from it.
chainlinkOracle.ethFeedPricesNothingNote: ARC PUBLISHES AN ETH/USD FEED AT 0x50FCDD99D6762D1C170DC6A9111db944AEE6D364 THAT PRICES NO TOKEN ON THIS CHAIN. It is a genuine feed - 9,571 bytes, 8 decimals, version 6, answer $2,606.66 - and there is nothing on Arc for it to price. The complete pool scan found no ETH representation in any form: all 52 ETH-or-BTC-family symbols were read and 51 are 18-decimal squatters worth under $452, and Circle's whole Arc token set, enumerated from MinterConfigured and MasterMinterChanged across all history, is USDC, EURC, cirBTC, USYC, MXNB, TRYB and three unnamed. There is no cirETH. A PUBLISHED FEED IS EVIDENCE ABOUT CHAINLINK COVERAGE, NOT EVIDENCE THAT AN ASSET TRADES HERE - do not infer a basket from a feed list. The 4663 two-asset basket does not port.
chainlinkOracle.proofOfReserveTrap: A PROOF-OF-RESERVE FEED SITS WHERE THE PRICE FEED SHOULD BE, AND IT SORTS FIRST. Chainlink publishes 'cirBTC Reserves' at 0xEB0884a871ea1f6483B5FC10fd3D7dC5806411fc: 9,571 bytes, decimals 8, version 6, a fresh positive answer - structurally indistinguishable from a price feed by every check except its description. It reports 786.98 (BTC in reserve) where CBBTC/USD reports 81,110.58 (dollars). It is the ONLY Arc feed whose description contains the basket asset's ticker, so it ranks first when the feed list is searched for cirBTC. ChainlinkOracle._requireUsdQuote REJECTS IT, and that rejection was mutation-tested eight ways against the real contract including the direction that matters: change ONLY the description to 'cirBTC / USD' and the identical feed is ACCEPTED. So the description check is what saves this, and the sane-price band is not. Populate feedDescriptionOnChain as base-mainnet.json does. Separately, XAUM's feed reports 18 decimals, so require(d == 8) rejects it independently and XAUM is not configurable without a contract change.

unresolved.basketShape: AN OWNER DECISION, NOT A LOOKUP - this is the one thing still blocking a deploy. Arc has exactly one basket-eligible non-stable asset, cirBTC, and no ETH representation at all. The 4663 design was a two-asset WETH + cbBTC basket, and that shape is unavailable here. The options are: a single-asset cirBTC vault; cirBTC plus a thin second leg from Arc's remaining Circle tokens, none of which is a crypto index constituent; or not launching the index on Arc yet. docs/SWARM.md section 10 puts launch parameters on the escalate list, so this is the owner's call and no session should pick one.
unresolved.sanePriceBand: Not chosen. ChainlinkOracle's constructor takes a band per asset and config-doc-truth.test.mjs enforces one for every *-mainnet.json under contracts/config/.
unresolved.heartbeat: See heartbeatChoiceNote - 86,400 s is a placeholder at MAX_HEARTBEAT, not an answer.
unresolved.sequencerPolicy: See sequencerUptimeFeedNote - DeployChainlinkOracle.s.sol must be widened deliberately.
unresolved.consequence: The router, the settlement token, the chain binding and the BTC leg are now established and read off chain. What is NOT established is what the basket should BE, the price band, the heartbeat and the sequencer policy - four decisions, of which the first is the owner's and the rest follow from it.

arcTestnetIsNotADeployTarget: MEASURED, AND IT RULES OUT THE OBVIOUS DRY RUN. Arc testnet (chain 5042002, https://rpc.testnet.arc.io, confirmed live at block 62,771,753) carries the USDC predeploy at the same address with the same 1,798 bytes and 6 decimals, Permit2 and Multicall3 — and NOTHING ELSE this protocol needs. Read on 5042002: canonical UniswapV3Factory 0 bytes, canonical SwapRouter02 0 bytes, UniversalRouter 0 bytes, Pyth receiver 0 bytes, CCTP TokenMessengerV2 0 bytes; and Chainlink's feed directory has no arc testnet network at all. `ChainlinkOracle` requires a genuine feed per asset and fails closed when it cannot produce a trustworthy price, so there is nothing on Arc testnet to point it at. A deploy there could only be made to stand up against mock feeds and a mock router, which would demonstrate that the bytecode is chain-portable and nothing whatsoever about oracle or execution behaviour.
deployAuthorisationNote: NO DEPLOY IS AUTHORISED BY THIS FILE. `docs/SWARM.md` §10 puts anything needing a private key, a funded account or `--broadcast` on the escalate-do-not-act list, together with mainnet deploys and fund movement. This file was written by a session holding no key and no funded account on 5042, and it is configuration evidence for a decision that remains the owner's.
whatThisFileIs: A SURVEY OF CHAIN 5042, NOT A DEPLOYABLE CONFIGURATION, and it is filed here rather than in contracts/config/ for exactly that reason. scripts/test/config-doc-truth.test.mjs enumerates every *-mainnet.json under contracts/config/ and holds it to the ChainlinkOracle constructor bounds: a resolved asset address per priced asset, a sane-price band, and feed decimals. This file now has the asset address and the router, but it has no band and - more fundamentally - no agreed basket, because Arc offers only one eligible asset. Putting it under contracts/config/ would still mean inventing a band or weakening that guard, and the guard is right: an incomplete mainnet config is not a mainnet config. WHEN the basket shape is decided and a band is chosen, this graduates into contracts/config/arc-mainnet.json and the guard covers it from that day.
